title: Kelantan
capsule: The Sultanate of Kelantan is a Malay kingdom on the northeastern coast of the Malay Peninsula whose ruling Long Yunus dynasty emerged in the mid-eighteenth century after a period of competing chieftainships and intermittent Siamese suzerainty. By the early nineteenth century Kelantan paid tribute to Bangkok while maintaining its own sultan and court traditions. Under the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909, Siam transferred its suzerainty over Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, and Perlis to Britain; a formal British advisor was installed in 1910, placing Kelantan within the Unfederated Malay States structure until Malayan independence in 1957.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Post-1909 boundaries are treaty-defined and reliable; the earlier territorial limits under Siamese suzerainty were fluid and documented only approximately in treaties and colonial surveys.
